claim_ceiling: Literature-reported metrics and public dataset metadata only. None of the model results below has been independently reproduced by this project. Results on different engines, datasets, label sets, source domains and split protocols are not directly comparable.

baselines.title: A universal transfer learning framework for cross-working-condition marine diesel engine fault diagnosis based on fine-tuning strategy
baselines.data_domain: Two marine diesel engine case studies: an 8V396SE engine (500 kW) and a 620 V16 engine (2336 kW); lubrication-system fault data include experimental bench evidence and intake/exhaust fault data include virtual simulation.

The evaluation is cross-domain simulation-to-bench, not multi-vessel shipboard validation.

Benchmark against source-only, target-only, fine-tuning, DANN, adaptive multi-source weighting and a calibrated non-neural baseline under exactly matched task groups.

baselines.title: A Digital Twin Framework for Monitoring and Fault Identification of Marine Internal Combustion Engines
baselines.data_domain: Calibrated 0D–1D thermodynamic model with experimental measurements from a Weichai WP4 marine diesel generator test bench, including in-cylinder pressure and vibration; constant-speed operation with three electrical-load reference modes and a controlled intake restriction.
baselines.task: Digital-twin calibration, operating-mode identification and inverse identification of physical factors responsible for deviations between modelled and measured marine-engine behaviour.

reported_metrics.value: controlled intake restriction on Weichai WP4 generator
reported_metrics.context: The framework is demonstrated using experimentally acquired test-bench data and a controlled intake restriction introduced by a throttle valve; it is not a fleet validation.
The authors distinguish an online data-connected diagnostic architecture from a continuously synchronized real-time twin; model execution is initiated through the diagnostic workflow.

baselines.split_protocol: Physics-model calibration around a small set of steady operating modes, followed by inverse identification using measured operating parameters and a controlled intake restriction. No train/test split or common ML leaderboard protocol is reported in the accessible methods.
reported_limitations: The authors explicitly identify practical non-uniqueness of the inverse problem: different physical-factor combinations can produce similar observable engine responses.
The experimental demonstration uses one Weichai WP4 generator test bench and a controlled intake restriction; it does not establish shipboard fleet validity or cross-engine transfer.
The accessible article does not report a directly comparable event-level diagnostic accuracy or fleet false-alarm rate.
The current workflow is online-data-connected but not continuously synchronized at a fixed real-time update frequency.
audit_notes: Important physical-model and inverse-problem comparator: tests a physical test-bench model rather than only a simulated engine.
Use as a baseline for model calibration, regime-conditioned reference generation, inverse-solution ambiguity and identifiability reporting.

Symtropy's differentiator should be explicit equivalence/ambiguity classes, evidence-bound parameter hypotheses, and qualification freshness—not an unsupported claim that the digital twin is more accurate.

baselines.title: A digital twin-enhanced deep metric learning framework for few-shot combustion fault diagnosis in marine diesel engines
baselines.data_domain: 0D/1D MATLAB/Simulink thermodynamic digital twin of a Wärtsilä 6L20 marine diesel engine, with three parametrically injected combustion-fault classes and physics-informed thermodynamic features.
baselines.task: Few-shot cross-condition combustion-fault classification using digital-twin pretraining, 128-dimensional Siamese metric embeddings and target-condition fine-tuning.

reported_metrics.context: Mean and standard deviation over 10 runs under the reported cycle-level leakage-free split, with K=20 target examples per class.
Triplet-only ablation in the same reported K=20 setting; higher than the proposed joint-loss result, so the joint objective is not the best reported variant in this setting.
Average accuracy reported under combined noise and speed-fluctuation interference across 25–100% maximum continuous rating loads.
Three typical combustion fault classes are parametrically injected into the 0D/1D digital-twin model.

baselines.split_protocol: Cycle-level leakage-free split; digital-twin source-condition pretraining and fine-tuning on K target-condition samples per class. Results are reported over 10 runs for the K=20 setting.
reported_limitations: The paper describes a simulation-based foundation using a thermodynamic digital twin and parametrically injected faults, not real-vessel fault recordings.
At K=20 the triplet-only ablation reports 90.91% accuracy, exceeding the proposed joint triplet–center loss method at 87.05% ± 5.14 percentage points.
The authors state that the primary contribution is physics-informed feature augmentation and data-efficient two-stage training, not a claim of state-of-the-art accuracy.
Source code and a sample dataset are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request; they are not described as a public reproducible archive.
audit_notes: Use for matched few-shot K-shot and cross-condition reproduction, not a physical-validation claim.
A fair comparison must reproduce the triplet-only ablation, use the same cycle-level holdout and report uncertainty over independent runs.
The 128-dimensional learned embedding is not itself evidence of physical fault identifiability or calibrated confidence.

baselines.title: Explainable AI-based root-cause diagnosis of maritime engine anomalies with external factors
baselines.data_domain: 18 months of actual operational data from one container ship; internal main-engine sensor time series plus external operational/environmental factors including wind-wave height, draft/trim and sea-surface temperature.
baselines.task: Unsupervised internal-engine anomaly detection using a variational autoencoder, clustering of internal anomaly patterns, and external Root Cause Anomaly Predictor (LightGBM) to predict anomaly scores from external/context variables; SHAP feature attribution used to interpret associations.

reported_metrics.context: One container ship; exact vessel identity, fleet coverage and operating-hour denominator require full methods/data audit.
Anomalies identified from internal engine sensor patterns; the abstract does not establish 335 independently adjudicated physical faults.
Four anomaly types were produced by hierarchical clustering of internal sensor patterns.
External variables associated with the VAE anomaly score by the RCAP LightGBM model and interpreted using SHAP; these are predictive associations, not identified causal effects.

baselines.split_protocol: The accessible abstract confirms an 18-month operational dataset and VAE→RCAP→SHAP pipeline but does not disclose a full vessel/run/time split, prospective holdout, leakage protocol, event adjudication procedure or independent-vessel test. Recover the full methods and split tables before reproduction.
reported_limitations: The operational validation is one container ship; it does not establish cross-vessel or cross-engine transfer.
The 335 anomaly events are detected/clustered internal-sensor patterns, not necessarily independently confirmed component faults or maintenance findings.

RCAP predicts the VAE anomaly score from external operational/environmental variables; SHAP explains predictive associations and does not by itself identify causal effects or prove that changing an external variable would change the engine anomaly.
The accessible abstract does not disclose time-split design, event adjudication, uncertainty/calibration, false-alarm exposure denominator or independent reproduction artifacts.
External context requires source/issuer, spatial alignment, valid-time and available-time provenance; the abstract-level description does not establish these details.
audit_notes: Important real-ship external-context comparator; it establishes a useful engine-monitoring capability beyond engine-internal signals.
Reproduce internal VAE anomaly score first, then external-only RCAP, naive feature fusion and context-conditioned models on frozen chronological splits.

Benchmark predictive association separately from causal attribution. Use time-aware and route/spatial negative controls, context permutation within matched operating strata, and prospective interventions only where independently authorized.

Symtropy differentiator: context evidence admission with source availability, valid time, spatial scope, clock uncertainty and dependency lineage, followed by explicit CONTEXT_ASSOCIATION_ONLY unless a causal design supports stronger claims.

baselines.title: AI/ML Based Anomaly Detection and Fault Diagnosis of Turbocharged Marine Diesel Engines: Experimental Study on Engine of an Operational Vessel
baselines.data_domain: In-service 1.89 MW Hyundai HiMSEN 4-stroke 900 RPM auxiliary generator on a cargo/container vessel. Healthy operational data were collected over two years across vessel engines; two reversible fouling faults (turbocharger nozzle-ring clogging and intercooler/charge-air-path restriction) were induced on one auxiliary engine at 825, 900 and 975 kW. Operational/thermodynamic values were captured non-intrusively from engine-room display screens; one single-axis vibration accelerometer per engine sampled at 20 kHz. The fault-class dataset has 96,897 observations and 42 features; fault observations are about 1.3% of the full sample set.
baselines.task: Healthy-only anomaly detection with undercomplete/stacked autoencoders, plus supervised seven-class severity diagnosis (healthy, three nozzle-ring clogging severities, three intercooler-clogging severities) using SVM and tree/nearest-neighbour baselines.

reported_metrics.context: Reported SVM balanced accuracy for seven-class severity classification on the paper's 80/20 data split; the paper also reports 10-fold cross-validation. The split is not shown as grouped by fault intervention, operating period or physical engine.

Reported balanced accuracy for combined nozzle-ring and intercooler clogging anomaly detection; F1 is 83.84% and ordinary accuracy is 98.15%. The dataset is highly imbalanced, so ordinary accuracy is not the appropriate headline.
Combined nozzle-ring and intercooler clogging anomaly detection; event-level metrics and false alarms per valid engine-hour are not reported.
Intercooler-clogging anomaly detection; UAE baseline is 51.55% balanced accuracy and 6.04% F1. The weaker early/low-severity fault is a useful negative-control target.
The paper reports that failure observations represent about 1.3% of the 96,897-point dataset; class prevalence materially affects ordinary accuracy.
Healthy data were collected over two years; this does not imply two years of labeled faults or two years of held-out deployment evaluation.

Nozzle-ring clogging (4/6/8 of 24 channels blocked) and intercooler/charge-air restriction (20/40/60% flow-area restriction); only one of the ship's auxiliary engines was used for the fault interventions.
The induced-fault experiments were performed at three steady auxiliary-engine load points, all below 52% of rated 1.89 MW; dynamic load transients and broader load coverage were excluded.

baselines.split_protocol: The study reports an 80/20 training/test split and 10-fold cross-validation for the seven-class supervised diagnosis task. The accessible description does not establish grouping by intervention/campaign, chronological block, engine or vessel; no independent-vessel holdout is reported. The healthy-only anomaly model uses healthy reference data, with threshold selection based on healthy reconstruction-loss distribution. Exact grouping, temporal leakage, preprocessing-fit and threshold-calibration boundaries must be recovered from the authors/data before reproduction.
reported_limitations: The fault experiments were induced on one 1.89 MW auxiliary engine on one cargo/container vessel, with only two fault mechanisms and three severity levels each; this is operational-vessel evidence but not a multi-vessel fleet benchmark.
The fault campaign covered three steady loads (825, 900, 975 kW); the authors explicitly excluded dynamic load transients.

The 80/20 split and 10-fold CV are reported, but the accessible paper does not disclose grouping by intervention, recording/run or chronology. Randomly split correlated windows could overstate generalization; this is an audit question, not an allegation of leakage.

The diagnostic corpus is highly imbalanced (about 1.3% fault observations); ordinary accuracy is not an adequate operational metric. The 99.72% SVM balanced accuracy is a paper-reported result, not an independently reproduced or cross-vessel result.

The paper's abstract labels the SAE result as 87.6% accuracy, while the detailed combined-fault results report 98.15% ordinary accuracy and 87.57% balanced accuracy; use the table's metric-specific values and preserve the distinction.

The paper identifies the 2026 data availability as subject to institutional/partner data-sharing agreements and available only on request under specific conditions; it is not a public benchmark payload.

Thermodynamic values were extracted non-intrusively from engine-room display screens; the authors identify future work on detailed uncertainty analysis and long-term comparison against direct digital interfaces.
The vessel experiment did not establish sensor-level independence or fault-to-capability qualification under common-cause loss.
audit_notes: Important higher-tier comparator because faults were physically induced on an in-service vessel engine, unlike purely simulated studies. Preserve this evidence stratum separately from test-bench and simulation results.

Reproduce the 99.72% balanced-accuracy SVM result and 80/20/10-fold protocol first, then run chronological blocks and intervention/run-grouped holdout. Do not treat the paper's score as cross-engine or fleet SOTA.
Reproduce the weak intercooler-only SAE result (75% balanced accuracy, 63.1% F1) and the UAE negative control (51.55% balanced accuracy, 6.04% F1); report severity-specific recall and uncertainty.
Use matched fault-free exposure and valid engine-hour denominators to report false alarms per engine-hour, plus event recall, latency, Brier/log score, risk-coverage and false-known/OOD rates.
Run leave-one-load-point-out only within the available 825/900/975 kW steady points; separate this from chronological and intervention-held-out experiments. Do not infer dynamic-transient support.
Evaluate the paper's modality contributions: display-extracted thermodynamics only, vibration only, and fused inputs; preserve each signal's acquisition fidelity/uncertainty and dependency topology.

Symtropy differentiator is not to claim >99.72% classification. It is to reproduce the strong score under the original protocol, then qualify whether it survives harder grouped splits, rare-fault conditions, calibration, ambiguity, sensor/common-cause loss and configuration changes.

baselines.title: Out-of-distribution challenges in intelligent fault diagnosis: a survey of generalization and detection
baselines.data_domain: 161 primary mechanical OOD-related fault-diagnosis studies coded by shift type and deployment role, including operating-condition, equipment, sensing-environment and fault-semantic changes.
baselines.task: Survey deployment-relative known-class generalization and unknown-fault/OOD detection, distinguishing condition shift (C-shift), fault-semantic shift (F-shift) and combined C+F settings.

reported_metrics.context: Primary mechanical OOD-related studies included and coded after screening.
Records remaining after deduplication from 280 database search records.
Records retrieved from IEEE Xplore, Web of Science and Scopus for 1 January 2020 through 16 July 2026.

baselines.split_protocol: Reproducible literature search and coding; not a diagnostic model experiment. The survey operationalizes deployment settings by effective training support, training label space and declared deployment envelope.
reported_limitations: A literature survey, not a trained model or a quantitative leaderboard result.
Its scope focuses on mechanical OOD-related diagnosis and does not claim exhaustive coverage of all closed-set domain adaptation, general anomaly detection or non-mechanical process monitoring.
Survey-reported methods and scores are not directly comparable without reproducing their specific data, task and split protocols.
audit_notes: Make C-shift, F-shift and C+F separate benchmark axes; a held-out load is not equivalent to an unseen fault semantic.
Evaluate known-class generalization separately from unknown-fault detection, then evaluate their integrated selective/escalation policy.
Require calibrated OOD disposition and explicit human-referral/unknown outputs rather than treating closed-set classifier confidence as diagnostic certainty.

baselines.title: Zero-Shot-Motivated Intelligent Fault Diagnosis: A Survey of Methods, Applications, and Future Directions
baselines.data_domain: Industrial fault-diagnosis zero-shot literature spanning target-semantic and domain-relation scenarios, priors, semantic alignment and unseen fault recognition.
baselines.task: Survey zero-shot-motivated fault diagnosis scenarios, methods, priors, evaluation goals and deployment limitations.

reported_metrics.context: Four scenarios distinguished by target semantics and domain relations: SD-UFC, SD-CFA, CD-UFC and CD-CFA.
Zero-target-shot and zero-fault-shot settings are distinguished as separate cases.
The review identifies a lack of scenario-aligned evaluation and reporting standards as a field limitation.

baselines.split_protocol: Literature survey based primarily on Google Scholar with forward/backward citation chasing and venue-based checks; no common dataset, model split or leaderboard is reported.
reported_limitations: The survey's literature collection is structured but not claimed to be an exhaustive systematic database review.
It does not provide a directly comparable marine-engine accuracy result.
Zero-shot claims depend on precisely defining target-domain data access, target fault semantics and the priors available at prediction time.
audit_notes: Use its scenario taxonomy to distinguish zero target labels, zero target data, unseen fault classes and cross-domain unseen-fault cases.
Require a declared prior/catalogue version, prior provenance, known/unknown label spaces, target-domain access rules and threshold-calibration scope for every zero-shot benchmark.
Do not call ordinary unsupervised domain adaptation zero-shot; disclose whether unlabeled target data or fault descriptions are available.

baselines.title: Towards adaptive closed-loop optimization: A review of sensor placement for digital twins in mechanical systems
baselines.data_domain: Review of optimal sensor placement for mechanical-system digital twins across lifecycle stages and multi-objective instrumentation requirements.
baselines.task: Review adaptive digital-twin-driven sensor placement, including virtual pre-placement, online performance evaluation and triggered re-optimization.

reported_metrics.context: Virtual-space pre-placement; data-model fusion and calibration; performance evaluation; triggered re-optimization; software-defined adaptive placement adjustment.
The review contrasts lifecycle-adaptive sensor placement with static one-time open-loop design.
Model generalization, real-time computational performance and completeness of the closed loop are highlighted as challenges.

baselines.split_protocol: Review article; it proposes a methodological framework and does not report a common physical engine diagnostic dataset, held-out validation split or comparative fleet performance result.
reported_limitations: A review/framework source, not an empirical improvement measurement.
The authors identify unresolved real-time, model-generalization and full-loop integration challenges.
Dynamic sensor redesign must remain constrained by physical installation, calibration, safety and engineering authorization; the review does not validate autonomous maritime sensor reconfiguration.
audit_notes: Use for the next programme stage: configuration-bound sensor-layout requalification when assets, faults, operating regimes or diagnostics change.
Treat layout updates as engineering proposals requiring review, not automatic installation or activation.
Benchmark trigger quality, re-optimization latency, Pareto-front stability, calibration burden and retained diagnosability separately.

baselines.title: Reliability-Aware Diagnostic Status Formation for Marine Diesel Engine Fault Diagnosis Under Noisy and Incomplete Evidence
baselines.data_domain: 3500-DEFault diesel-engine fault-feature benchmark generated from a simulated engine model, evaluated at fixed 2500 rpm across 0, 15, 30 and 60 dB SNR. Four operational classes are reconstructed from simulated fault/severity variables; scenarios are split into train, calibration, validation and final test.
baselines.task: Post-prediction D0-D5 diagnostic status formation using calibrated class probabilities, predicted severity, pressure/torsion feature-group consistency and evidence completeness; compared against calibrated-confidence, probability-margin and entropy rejection baselines.

reported_metrics.context: Reported over five split seeds after scenario-disjoint train/calibration/validation/test partitioning; the benchmark remains simulated and fixed-speed.
Coverage of the proposed D0-D5 status layer across the reported final-test repetitions.
Four-class selective risk for the status layer. Approximately matched entropy rejection reports slightly lower risk, so superiority in rejection efficiency is not claimed.
Compared with the forced classifier false-safe rate of 0.0094 ± 0.0038. This is a simulated benchmark measure, not a validated shipboard false-safe rate.
Reference forced-classification false-safe rate used in the paper's comparison.
Fraction of true G4 cases assigned D3/D4 by the proposed status layer.
Approximately coverage-matched entropy rejection has slightly lower selective risk than the proposed status layer; the article explicitly does not claim superior rejection efficiency.

baselines.split_protocol: Scenario-disjoint training, calibration, validation and final-test partitions; operating parameters selected on validation data and locked before final-test evaluation; five split seeds quantify split sensitivity but do not represent independent engine replications.
reported_limitations: The 3500-DEFault source data are generated by a simulated diesel-engine model, not operational shipboard or physical engine recordings.
All reported scenarios use a fixed 2500 rpm operating speed; variable-speed and maneuvering generalization are not established.
Five split seeds quantify sensitivity to the split, not replication across independent physical engines or vessels.
The proposed status layer's approximately coverage-matched entropy-rejection baseline has slightly lower selective risk; the authors do not claim superior rejection efficiency.
Partial torsional-feature loss exposed severe-case underwarning without universal refusal; feature-group completeness therefore requires explicit severity-stratified stress testing.
The D0-D5 states are rule-derived diagnostic indications and are not independently validated maintenance states or maintenance decisions.
audit_notes: Useful competitive baseline for calibrated post-prediction diagnostic status, evidence completeness, severity-aware underwarning and false-safe admission.
Reproduce forced prediction, confidence/margin/entropy rejection, and proposed D0-D5 layer at approximately matched coverage before comparing selective risk.
Report false-safe rate and severe-case underwarning separately from ordinary classification accuracy; include partial pressure-group and torsional-group dropout.
Do not conflate D0-D5 diagnostic indications with engine operating status, maintenance authorization, vessel ODD status or permission to operate.

baselines.title: Control-aware affine network: a novel framework for reliable fault diagnosis of marine diesel engines in dynamic maneuvers
baselines.data_domain: Proprietary marine-diesel injector-system simulation data covering dynamic maneuvering conditions. The authors state that the simulation data and self-developed engine model are not publicly shareable under industrial confidentiality and IP restrictions.
baselines.task: Control-aware feature calibration using real-time control signals, followed by dual-feature decoupling into fault-severity and maneuver-invariant representations using knowledge distillation and adversarial training.

reported_metrics.context: The accessible abstract describes the architecture and simulated cross-maneuvering evaluation but does not provide a numeric accuracy, false-alarm, calibration or transfer score.

The authors state that simulation datasets and the self-developed simulation model are withheld under industrial confidentiality and internal intellectual-property restrictions; partial de-identified analytical results may be requested by eligible researchers.

baselines.split_protocol: The accessible abstract reports evaluation across cross-maneuvering tasks using diesel-engine injection-system simulations. Exact scenario/engine split identities, task-level scores, calibration protocol and leakage controls require full-methods audit; the simulation data and model are not publicly available.
reported_limitations: The reported evaluation uses marine diesel injection-system simulations, not physical engine or shipboard records.
The simulation model, parameterization and datasets are not publicly released, limiting independent reproduction.
The accessible abstract does not expose numerical performance metrics, per-maneuver results or uncertainty/calibration evidence.
The claimed maneuver-invariant representation must be tested against residual fault-severity loss and negative transfer, not only cross-domain average accuracy.
audit_notes: Important comparator to simple control-signal concatenation and control-aware domain-adversarial fusion: control signals are used as calibration mechanisms, then severity and maneuver-invariant features are decoupled.
Symtropy should compare command-conditioned residual models, CAAN-style feature calibration, severity retention and unknown-regime abstention under matched held-out maneuvering scenarios.
Do not infer superiority or reproduce a score until source methods, dataset access and target splits are available.

baselines.title: Transformer-enhanced feature extraction with adaptive thresholding for domain generalization fault diagnosis under open-set scenarios
baselines.data_domain: Three public bearing datasets; 16 open-set domain-generalization fault-diagnosis tasks spanning known-class recognition, domain shift and unknown-fault rejection.
baselines.task: Open-set domain-generalization using transformer-enhanced fault embeddings, magnitude/orientation decoupling, hyperspherical feature constraints and sample-wise adaptive rejection thresholds.

reported_metrics.context: Overall H-score reported across 16 open-set domain-generalization tasks and three public bearing datasets; not a marine-engine or vessel result.

baselines.split_protocol: The accessible abstract reports 16 OSDGFD tasks over three public bearing datasets. Per-task source/target/fault holdout details must be extracted and reproduced before direct comparison.
reported_limitations: The demonstrated datasets are bearings, not marine diesel engines or shipboard propulsion machinery.
The 94.74% average H-score is paper-reported and has not been independently reproduced.
No real marine-engine or vessel validation is established by this result.
audit_notes: Useful current open-set domain-generalization comparator and H-score reference.
Reproduce with the same unknown-fault and unseen-condition partition before comparing numbers.
Our maritime benchmark should add false-known rate, worst-domain H-score, calibration and ambiguity reporting rather than optimizing only aggregate H-score.

baselines.title: SEE–GROW: Reliable exploration and boundary-aware learning for open-set single-domain generalization in fault diagnosis
baselines.data_domain: Bearing and planetary-gearbox rotating-machinery datasets; open-set tests under unseen operating conditions.
baselines.task: Open-set single-domain generalization that diversifies known-class support, synthesizes boundary-adjacent pseudo-unknown examples, shapes known/unknown separation and distills uncertainty-aware rejection.

reported_metrics.value: authors report improvement over SOTA; numeric value not present in accessible abstract
reported_metrics.context: The paper reports harmonic-mean improvement between known-fault recognition and unknown-fault detection under unseen operating conditions.

baselines.split_protocol: Single-domain generalization with unknown-fault rejection under unseen operating conditions; exact fault-family and operating-domain holdouts need method-level reproduction.
reported_limitations: The public abstract does not provide a numeric score suitable for a matched leaderboard comparison.
The demonstrated domains are generic rotating machinery rather than marine diesel engines.
Pseudo-unknown synthesis and rejection boundaries require independent sensitivity tests for false-known and false-unknown errors.
audit_notes: Benchmark known-fault recognition and unknown-fault detection jointly, using a harmonic metric plus separate component metrics.
Do not assume the pseudo-unknown generator covers physically plausible marine fault families.
Retain calibration, worst-domain and false-known gates.

baselines.title: Prototype-driven open-set domain generalization for rotating machinery fault diagnosis via multiview adversarial purification
baselines.data_domain: Three public rotating-machinery datasets: SDUST planetary gearbox, HUST parallel gearbox and HIT aero-engine bearing; native multi-axis or multi-location signals are treated as physically complementary views.
baselines.task: Open-set domain generalization with multiview adversarial purification, cross-view consistency, hyperspherical class geometry and prototype-driven pseudo-OOD synthesis.

reported_metrics.context: SDUST planetary gearbox, HUST parallel gearbox and HIT aero-engine bearing.

reported_metrics.value: authors report superiority to SOTA; no single numeric aggregate transcribed
reported_metrics.context: The authors report improvements in diagnostic accuracy and open-set rejection under complex operating conditions.

baselines.split_protocol: Multi-domain open-set generalization across the three named datasets. Exact source/target domains, unknown-class splits and per-dataset metrics must be reconstructed from the paper and public implementation.
reported_limitations: No marine diesel or vessel dataset is used.
Cross-view agreement can reinforce common-mode disturbances if physical measurement dependencies are not represented; the paper's multiview representation is not itself proof of independent evidence.
The reported performance has not been independently reproduced in Symtropy.
audit_notes: This is a particularly relevant method comparator for physically grounded multiview diagnosis.
Our adapter must count independent measurement principles and dependency groups, not raw channel count or view count.
Use native multiaxis/multilocation marine sensor data only after verifying instrumentation and shared power, clock and acquisition dependencies.

baselines.title: Domain-augmented open-set generalization framework for fault diagnosis in rotating machinery
baselines.data_domain: Generic rotating-machinery bearing/gearbox fault diagnosis under working-condition shifts and unknown fault types.
baselines.task: Target-free open-set domain generalization combining frequency-domain multi-source interpolation, WGAN-GP pseudo-unknown synthesis and reconstruction-based feature learning with a physics-informed spectral constraint.

reported_metrics.context: Paper-reported result on its own rotating-machinery datasets.
Paper-reported unknown-fault rejection rate on its own protocol; not comparable with TFEAT H-score.

baselines.split_protocol: Target-free open-set generalization under varying operating conditions; detailed dataset split and unknown-class protocol must be reconstructed for reproduction.
reported_limitations: The authors characterize the contribution as an integration-based advancement rather than a fundamentally new paradigm.
The 92.3% classification accuracy and 89.5% rejection rate come from a different task and dataset than the 94.74% TFEAT H-score; they must not be ranked directly.
No marine diesel engine or shipboard validation is established.
audit_notes: Use as a matched baseline for target-free open-set domain generalization and physics-informed feature constraints.
Report known-fault accuracy and unknown rejection separately, together with H-score, false-known rate and calibration.
